arxiv-2105-15201.title: Dynamics of superconducting qubit relaxation times
arxiv-2105-15201.creator: M. Carroll *, S. Rosenblatt *, P. Jurcevic, I. Lauer, A. Kandala
arxiv-2105-15201.description: Abstract Superconducting qubits are a leading candidate for quantum computing but display temporal fluctuations in their energy relaxation times T 1 T_{1} . This introduces instabilities in multi-qubit device performance. Furthermore, autocorrelation in these time fluctuations introduces challenges for obtaining representative measures of T 1 T_{1} for process optimization and device screening.

arxiv-2107-06500.title: Posterior sampling for inverse imaging problems on the sphere in seismology and cosmology
arxiv-2107-06500.creator: Augustin Marignier, 1,2 Jason D. McEwen, 1 Ana M. G. Ferreira, 2,3 Thomas D. Kitching 1 1 Mullard Space Science Laboratory, University College London, Dorking RH5 6NT, UK 2 Department of Earth Sciences, University College London, London WC1E 6BT, UK 3 CERIS, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade
arxiv-2107-06500.description: Abstract In this work, we describe a framework for solving spherical inverse imaging problems using posterior sampling for full uncertainty quantification. Inverse imaging problems defined on the sphere arise in many fields, including seismology and cosmology where images are defined on the globe and the cosmic sphere, and are generally high-dimensional and computationally expensive.

arxiv-2110-05758.title: Role of Externally Provided Randomness in Stochastic Teams and Zero-sum Team Games
arxiv-2110-05758.creator: Rahul Meshram
arxiv-2110-05758.description: Abstract Stochastic team decision problem is extensively studied in literature and the existence of optimal solution is obtained in recent literature. The value of information in statistical problem and decision theory is classical problem. Much of earlier does not qualitatively describe role of externally provided private and common randomness in stochastic team problem and team vs team zero sum game.

arxiv-2111-14285.title: Early Stage Growth of Amorphous Thin Film: Average Kinetics, Nanoscale Dynamics and Pressure Dependence
arxiv-2111-14285.creator: Chenyu Wang, Karl F. Ludwig, Jr, Christa Wagenbach, Meliha G. Rainville, Suresh Narayanan, Hua Zhou, Jeffrey G. Ulbrandt, Randall L. Headrick
arxiv-2111-14285.description: Abstract We used the Coherent Grazing Incidence Small Angle X-Ray Scattering (Co-GISAXS) technique to study the average kinetics and nanoscale dynamics during early-stage a-WSi 2 sputter deposition. The kinetic and dynamic properties are examined as a function of pressure, which is known to be a critical factor in determining final surface roughness.

arxiv-2206-05811.title: Semi-Annihilation of Fermionic Dark Matter
arxiv-2206-05811.creator: Priyotosh Bandyopadhyay, Debajyoti Choudhury, Divya Sachdeva
arxiv-2206-05811.description: Abstract The continued non-observation of events emanating from dark matter (DM) annihilations in various direct and indirect detection experiments calls into question the mechanism for determining the relic density of a weakly interacting massive particle. However, if the relic density is determined primarily by a semi-annihilation process, as opposed to the usual annihilation, this tension can be ameliorated.

arxiv-2210-16018.title: Code4ML: a Large-scale Dataset of annotated Machine Learning Code
arxiv-2210-16018.creator: Anastasia Drozdova, Polina Guseva, Ekaterina Trofimova, Anna Scherbakova, Andrey Ustyuzhanin, Ekaterina Trofimova
arxiv-2210-16018.description: Abstract Program code as a data source is gaining popularity in the data science community. Possible applications for models trained on such assets range from classification for data dimensionality reduction to automatic code generation. However, without annotation number of methods that could be applied is somewhat limited. To address the lack of annotated datasets, we present the Code4ML corpus.

arxiv-2305-01390.title: Large eddy simulation of a low-pressure turbine cascade with turbulent end wall boundary layers
arxiv-2305-01390.creator: Christian Morsbach, Michael Bergmann, Adem Tosun, Bjoern F. Klose, Edmund Kügeler, Matthias Franke
arxiv-2305-01390.description: Abstract We present results of implicit large eddy simulation (LES) and different Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) models of the MTU 161 low pressure turbine at an exit Reynolds number of 90,000 and exit Mach number of 0.6. The LES results are based on a high order discontinuous Galerkin method and the RANS is computed using a classical finite-volume approach.

arxiv-2305-09761.title: NerfBridge: Bringing Real-time, Online Neural Radiance Field Training to Robotics Thanks: *Corresponding Author: javieryu@stanford.edu . 1. Stanford University Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics 2. Stanford University Department of Mechanical Engineering. This work was funded in part by ONR
arxiv-2305-09761.creator: Javier Yu 1∗, Jun En Low 2, Keiko Nagami 1, Mac Schwager 1
arxiv-2305-09761.description: Abstract Neural radiance fields (NeRFs) are a class of implicit scene representations that model 3D environments from color images. NeRFs are expressive, and can model the complex and multi-scale geometry of real world environments, which potentially makes them a powerful tool for robotics applications.

arxiv-2402-13667.title: GCOF: Self-iterative Text Generation for Copywriting Using Large Language Model
arxiv-2402-13667.creator: Jianghui Zhou, Ya Gao, Jie Liu Xuemin Zhao, Zhaohua Yang, Yue Wu, Lirong Shi JingDong Technology {zhoujianghui, gaoya26, liujie365}@jd.com
arxiv-2402-13667.description: Abstract Large language models(LLM) such as ChatGPT have substantially simplified the generation of marketing copy, yet producing content satisfying domain specific requirements, such as effectively engaging customers, remains a significant challenge. In this work, we introduce the Genetic Copy Optimization Framework (GCOF) designed to enhance both efficiency and engagememnt of marketing copy creation.

arxiv-2508-13930.title: InPars+: Supercharging Synthetic Data Generation for Information Retrieval Systems
arxiv-2508-13930.creator: Matey Krastev, Miklos Hamar, Danilo Toapanta, Jesse Brouwers, Yibin Lei
arxiv-2508-13930.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Matey Krastev, Miklos Hamar, Danilo Toapanta, Jesse Brouwers, Yibin Lei. This work revisits and extends synthetic query generation pipelines for Neural Information Retrieval (NIR) by leveraging the InPars Toolkit, a reproducible, end-to-end framework for generating training data using large language models (LLMs). We first assess the reproducibility of the original InPars, InPars-V2, and Promptagator pipelines on the SciFact benchmark and validate their effectiveness using open-source reranker and generator models.

arxiv-2511-13653.title: Weight-sparse transformers have interpretable circuits
arxiv-2511-13653.creator: Leo Gao, Achyuta Rajaram, Jacob Coxon, Soham V. Govande, Bowen Baker, Dan Mossing
arxiv-2511-13653.description: Abstract Finding human-understandable circuits in language models is a central goal of the field of mechanistic interpretability. We train models to have more understandable circuits by constraining most of their weights to be zeros, so that each neuron only has a few connections.

pmc-10683969.title: Role of immunometabolism during congenital cytomegalovirus infection
pmc-10683969.creator: Kevin J Zwezdaryk, Amitinder Kaur
pmc-10683969.description: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a master manipulator of host metabolic pathways. The impact of CMV metabolic rewiring during congenital CMV on immune function is unknown. CMV infection can directly alter glycolytic and oxidative phosphorylation pathways in infected cells. Recent data suggests CMV may alter metabolism in uninfected neighboring cells.

pmc-11406037.title: Is lupus anticoagulant testing with dilute Russell’s viper venom clotting times reliable in the presence of inflammation?
pmc-11406037.creator: Michael Hardy, Emilie Catry, Marie Pouplard, Thomas Lecompte, François Mullier
pmc-11406037.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundTesting for lupus anticoagulant (LA) is not recommended in case of inflammation as C-reactive protein (CRP) can interfere in vitro with the phospholipids present in the activated partial thromboplastin time test used to detect an LA.

pmc-11494526.title: Biermer’s disease unveiled: Bilateral macular hemorrhage as a rare manifestation—A case report
pmc-11494526.creator: Ben Addou Idrissi Sara, Himmich Mohammed, Moutei Hassan, Bennis Ahmed, Chraibi Fouad, Abdellaoui Meriem, Benatiya Andaloussi Idriss
pmc-11494526.description: The patient, a 30-year-old woman, presented with a sudden, painless, and severe decrease in vision in both eyes. The ophthalmological examination revealed a normal anterior segment and intraocular pressure, but a fundus examination showed bilateral macular hemorrhage. In the absence of a known history, a metabolic and hematological biological assessment was conducted.

pmc-13586506.title: Lymphomatoid papulosis: a practical review for pathologists
pmc-13586506.creator: Mario L Marques-Piubelli, Carlos A Torres-Cabala, Roberto N Miranda
pmc-13586506.description: Lymphomatoid papulosis (LyP) is a primary cutaneous CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by a chronic and self-healing recurrent cluster of erythematous papules or nodules on the skin of the trunk and/or extremities. The disease has an indolent clinical course with spontaneous regression or waxing and waning clinical evolution.

pmc-13656483.title: A community-based qualitative study of perspectives on alcohol public health interventions and experiences of alcohol use
pmc-13656483.creator: Sarah Dance, Andrew Weyman, Sally Adams, Amy H Barton, Amber Burd, Naomi Nelson, Charlotte Dack
pmc-13656483.description: BackgroundThe alcohol harm paradox is where lower socioeconomic position (SEP) groups experience higher rates of alcohol-related health consequences than higher SEP populations, despite drinking less alcohol. The reasons behind this are not certain, and limited research has examined the acceptability of alcohol interventions.
